exam_scheme.note: The Joint CSIR-UGC NET Examination is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) on behalf of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) to determine eligibility for the award of Junior Research Fellowship (JRF), Lectureship (LS) / Assistant Professorship, and admission to Ph.D. programmes in Indian universities and colleges. The test covers five scientific disciplines: Chemical Sciences; Earth, Atmospheric, Ocean and Planetary Sciences; Life Sciences; Mathematical Sciences; and Physical Sciences. It is administered as a single-paper Computer Based Test (CBT) of 3 hours (180 minutes) carrying a maximum of 200 marks, structured into three parts: Part A (General Aptitude, common to all subjects), Part B (Subject-related conventional MCQs), and Part C (Higher-order scientific concept questions testing analytical reasoning). Negative marking applies at 25% across all parts.

stages.stage_name: Joint CSIR-UGC NET Computer Based Test (CBT)

papers.paper_name: Part A: General Science, Quantitative Aptitude & Research Reasoning (Common)
papers.negative_marking: -0.5 marks for each wrong answer (+2 for correct; attempt any 15 out of 20 questions)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Aggregate merit cutoff calculated across Parts A, B, and C combined

papers.paper_name: Part B: Subject-Related Core Multiple Choice Questions
papers.negative_marking: 25% negative marking for wrong answers (+2 for correct; subject-specific question options)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Aggregate merit cutoff calculated across Parts A, B, and C combined

papers.paper_name: Part C: Higher Order Scientific Problem Solving & Analytical Questions
papers.negative_marking: 25% negative marking for wrong answers (typically +4 or +4.75 marks per correct question)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Aggregate merit cutoff calculated across Parts A, B, and C combined
